key_insight: RECONTEXT shows that long-context reasoning can improve without retraining the model by repeatedly replaying the most relevant evidence into the LLM’s working context. Instead of just giving the model more text, it helps the model actually use the evidence already there.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the gap between having a long context window and effectively using information inside that context. Many LLMs can accept long inputs but still miss or underuse key evidence when making reasoning decisions.
method: A training-free inference harness that recursively replays evidence relevant to the current reasoning step.
Selects and re-injects supporting context so the model can focus on the most useful parts of the long input.
Improves long-context reasoning by guiding attention toward evidence rather than relying on the model to find it on its own.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical way to boost long-context performance without fine-tuning or changing the base model. It is especially useful for applications like document QA, multi-hop reasoning, and analysis over large documents or conversations.

paper_title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning
paper_authors: Yanjun Zhao, Ruizhong Qiu, Tianxin Wei, Yuanchen Bei, Zhining Liu
